correctness.rationale: For \(a_0=1\), submultiplicativity makes each Wallen ratio block admissible. At every finite extension, only finitely many new crossing products involve the newly inserted positive bridge, so that bridge can be chosen small enough to preserve every required upper bound. Repeating longer prefixes arbitrarily far out gives \(\|W^n\|=a_n\) and supplies an orthonormal weakly null sequence on which \(W^n\) has norm \(a_n\); compact operators vanish on that sequence, hence \(\|W^n\|_e=a_n\). Positive weights make the unilateral shift irreducible. For \(a_n=\rho_n^n\) with \(\rho_n\) nonincreasing, submultiplicativity is immediate and both spectral-radius formulas have the prescribed exact root values.
